info.title: MemOS Dashboard APIs
info.description: Dashboard API for managing messages and searching memories in MemOS.

post.description: This API allows you to add one or more messages to a specific conversation. As illustrated in the examples bellow, you can add messages in real time during a user-assistant interaction, import historical messages in bulk, or enrich the conversation with user preferences and behavior data. All added messages are transformed into memories by MemOS, enabling their retrieval in future conversations to support chat history management, user behavior tracking, and personalized interactions.

messages.content: I want to travel during summer vacation, can you recommend something?
Sure! Are you traveling alone, with family or with friends?
I'm bringing my kid. My family always travels together.
Got it, so you're traveling with your children as a family, right?
Yes, with both kids and elderly, we usually travel as a whole family.
Understood, I'll recommend destinations suitable for family trips.

post.description: This API retrieves the historical conversation records between a user and the assistant for a specified session, with the option to limit the number of results. As shown in the examples bellow, you can use the returned recent messages as references for the model when generating responses, maintaining dialogue coherence and contextual understanding. It can also be used to restore chat context when a user refreshes or reopens the app, ensuring a seamless user experience and supporting personalized interactions.
This API retrieves memories for a specified user or Agent and returns the fragments most relevant to the query.

example.query: Summarize my memories related to reading this year
What fun places are in Shanghai?

post.description: Retrieve paginated memories for a user or Agent.
Delete memories for a user or Agent. Supports deletion by memory_ids or clearing all memories by user_id/agent_id.
This API is used to add feedback to current session messages, allowing MemOS to correct memories based on user feedback.
Uses MemOS’s self-developed extraction model to extract and return fact and preference memories directly from conversation messages.

messages.content: I’ve planned a summer trip to Guangzhou. What chain hotels can you recommend for accommodation?
You can consider options like 7 Days Inn, All Seasons, Hilton, and others.
Alright—ask me anytime if you have more questions.

post.description: Provides a memory reranking API based on the memos-reranker small model. It takes a user query and a list of candidate memories and completes memory relevance reranking with a single call.

documents: User is a backend developer in Hangzhou.
User is going on a business trip to Beijing next Wednesday.

post.description: Query the processing status of async tasks such as add/message and add/feedback. When a task completes, the response includes memory_views with added/updated/deleted counts and memory IDs grouped by memory category.
Create a knowledgebase associated with the project.
Delete a knowledge base or remove its association with the current project.
Upload files to a specified Knowledge Base. By default, files are uploaded as documents. When file[].type is skill, upload a Markdown Skill file or ZIP Skill package.

Get file information in one of two ways: pass file_ids to retrieve specific file details, or pass knowledgebase_id to list files under a Knowledge Base. Choose only one mode; passing both knowledgebase_id and file_ids returns an error.
Delete files from a specified Knowledge Base. When a Skill file is deleted, the associated Skill is deleted as well.
Bind a Profile template to a user or Agent, creating a Profile memory instance. After binding, the corresponding attribute fields are automatically updated whenever new messages are added.

Edit a Profile memory instance: add fields, update field values, remove fields, or lock fields against automatic updates by the algorithm. Only the target instance is affected; the template and other instances are not changed.
Delete a user's or Agent's Profile memory instance. All field values and bindings for that instance are removed. This does not affect the template itself or other instances.
Manually update the content, title, or status of an existing memory. Supports all memory categories, including fact memories, preference memories, Event Memory, and Profile attribute values.

user_id.title: User ID
user_id.description: Unique identifier of the user associated with the conversation.

conversation_id.title: Conversation ID
conversation_id.description: Unique identifier of the conversation. Providing this clarifies the current session, prioritizing its memory over historical sessions. If omitted, cross-session memory retrieval is performed for more relevant responses.

filter.title: Filter
filter.description: Filter conditions, used to precisely limit the memory scope before retrieval. Available fields include: "agent_id", "app_id", "create_time", "update_time", and specific fields in "info". Supports logical operators (and, or) and comparison operators (gte, lte, gt, lt). For the "info" field, supports filtering by "business_type", "biz_id", "scene", and other custom fields.

knowledgebase_ids.title: Knowledgebase IDs
knowledgebase_ids.description: Specifies the scope of Knowledge Bases accessible for the current search. Defaults to empty, meaning no Knowledge Bases are searched. Pass specific Knowledge Base IDs to search ordinary documents and uploaded Skills in those Knowledge Bases; pass "all" to search across all associated Knowledge Bases within the project.

memory_limit_number.title: Memory Limit Number
memory_limit_number.description: Maximum number of memories that can be recalled: as long as the relevance threshold (relativity) is met, up to this many memories may be returned. Default is 9, maximum is 25.

include_preference.title: Include Preference
include_preference.description: Whether to recall preference memories. When enabled, the system intelligently recalls memories related to user preferences based on the query. Default = true.

preference_limit_number.title: Preference Limit Number
preference_limit_number.description: Maximum number of preferred memories that can be recalled: as long as the relevance threshold (relativity) is met, up to this many preference memories may be returned. Default is 9, maximum is 25.

relativity.title: Relativity
relativity.description: Relevance threshold (0–1) for recalled memories. Filters out low-relevance memories and, together with the maximum counts for factual and preferred recalls, constrains the final results. When omitted, the system default threshold is used. A value of 0 disables relevance filtering.

max_tokens.title: Max Tokens
max_tokens.description: Indicates the maximum number of generated tokens.

GetFileRequest.description: Supports two query modes: pass file_ids to retrieve specific file details; or pass knowledgebase_id to list files under a Knowledge Base, optionally with type, page, and page_size for filtering and pagination. Choose exactly one mode. Passing both knowledgebase_id and file_ids returns an error; passing neither also returns an error.

knowledgebase_id.title: Knowledgebase ID
knowledgebase_id.description: Query mode 1: target Knowledge Base ID. Returns files under the Knowledge Base and can be used with type, page, and page_size. Do not pass it together with file_ids.

type.title: Type
type.description: File type filter, effective only when querying by knowledgebase_id. document returns only ordinary documents; skill returns only Skill files; omit this field to return all files. Do not use it with the file_ids query mode.

page.title: Page
page.description: Page number, effective only when querying by knowledgebase_id. Do not use it with the file_ids query mode.

page_size.title: Page Size
page_size.description: Items per page, effective only when querying by knowledgebase_id. Do not use it with the file_ids query mode.

file_ids.title: File IDs
file_ids.description: Query mode 2: file ID list. Returns details for the specified files. When using this mode, pass only file_ids and do not pass knowledgebase_id, type, page, or page_size.

preference.title: Preference
preference.description: Concrete preference text extracted from the dialogue.

reasoning.title: Reasoning
reasoning.description: How this preference was inferred from the conversation.

preference_type.title: Preference Type
preference_type.description: explicit_preference: clearly stated by the user; implicit_preference: inferred from behavior or context.

memory_detail_list.title: Memory Detail List
memory_detail_list.description: Factual memories. Returned when the request includes memory in extraction_types, or when extraction_types is omitted.

preference_detail_list.title: Preference Detail List
preference_detail_list.description: Preference memories. Returned when the request includes preference in extraction_types, or when extraction_types is omitted; may mix explicit and implicit preferences.

documents.title: Documents

top_n.title: Top N
top_n.description: Return the top N most relevant results. If omitted, returns all results by default.

index.title: Index
index.description: The index position of this document in the original documents list.

text.title: Text
text.description: The original text content of the document.

relevance_score.title: Relevance Score
relevance_score.description: Relevance score, ranging from 0 to 1, higher indicates more relevant to the query.

prompt_tokens.title: Prompt Tokens
prompt_tokens.description: Number of tokens consumed by the prompt.

results.title: Results
results.description: List of reranked results, sorted in descending order by relevance_score.

messages.title: Messages
messages.description: Array of message objects from which to extract memories. The combined Token count of all messages must not exceed 8k.

extraction_types.title: Extraction Types
extraction_types.description:
Limits which memory types to extract; omit to extract all supported types.

  • memory: factual memories—user-related factual information extracted from the dialogue.
  • preference: preference memories—user preferences from the dialogue, including explicit preferences (clearly stated) and implicit preferences (inferred from behavior).
